standard_prerequisites.name: Determinant of a (2,1)-periodic complex and the characterization of it by a single symbol comparison
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, chow.tex, the definition of det_kappa(M, alpha, beta) for an exact (2, 1)-periodic complex and the subsequent characterisation results
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that det_kappa of an exact (2, 1)-periodic complex is an element of kappa^* and that it is uniquely determined by comparing two symbols, which is the form in which the three determinants are compared in the counted proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: The characterisation of the determinant by any admissible generating sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Remark labelled remark-more-elementary (source line 16632), invoked at proof lines 17065, 17077 and 17090
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the defining relation for D, D_1 and D_2 may be written with the particular admissible sequences chosen in the proof; the choice of those sequences, the length bookkeeping and the combination of the three relations stay inside the counted span.

core_obligations: Derive the exactness of (I_gamma, alpha, beta) from the two short exact sequences 0 -> I_{beta gamma} -> I_gamma -> I_{alpha gamma} -> 0 and 0 -> I_{alpha gamma} -> I_gamma -> I_{beta gamma} -> 0 that the hypotheses produce (proof lines 17016-17030).

Show that alpha and gamma induce well defined endomorphisms of M/K_beta and identify their kernels as I_gamma/K_beta and I_alpha/K_beta respectively, using alpha(I_{gamma alpha}) = I_{alpha gamma alpha} subset I_{alpha gamma} = K_beta (proof lines 17033-17041).

Set r = length_R(K_alpha), s = length_R(K_beta), t = length_R(K_gamma), record the four length identities, choose admissible sequences generating the three kernels together with lifts, and use the characterisation of the determinant to write D, D_1 and D_2 each as the unique scalar of a displayed symbol relation with signs (-1)^{r(s+t)}, (-1)^{rt} and (-1)^{rs} respectively, whose product gives D = D_1 D_2 (proof lines 17044-17103).
proof_roadmap: Exactness of the three periodic complexes: reduce to the two short exact sequences in I_gamma and to the computation of the kernels on M/K_beta (proof lines 17013-17041).
Length bookkeeping for the three kernels and the middle module (proof lines 17044-17049).
Choose the admissible sequences and lifts, then compare the three symbol relations and multiply out the determinants with their signs (proof lines 17050-17103).
difficulty_reason: Under the two kernel/image hypotheses I_alpha = K_{beta gamma} and K_alpha = I_{beta gamma} for every permutation of the three endomorphisms alpha, beta, gamma of a finite length module M over a local ring, the lemma asserts that three triples are exact (2, 1)-periodic complexes and that det_kappa(M, alpha, beta gamma) = det_kappa(I_gamma, alpha, beta) det_kappa(M/K_beta, alpha, gamma) (statement lines 16982-17010). The exactness parts are reductions through specifically constructed short exact sequences 0 -> I_{beta gamma} -> I_gamma -> I_{alpha gamma} -> 0 and 0 -> I_{alpha gamma} -> I_gamma -> I_{beta gamma} -> 0 (proof lines 17016-17030) together with the check alpha(K_beta) subset K_beta, gamma(K_beta) subset K_beta computed as alpha(I_{gamma alpha}) = I_{alpha gamma alpha} subset I_{alpha gamma} = K_beta (proof lines 17033-17041). The determinant identity itself is not a computation with the definition: the author chooses admissible sequences x, y, z generating K_alpha, K_beta, K_gamma together with lifts x-tilde, y-tilde, z-tilde, records the length bookkeeping length_R(I_alpha) = s + t, length_R(I_beta) = r + t, length_R(I_gamma) = r + s and length_R(M) = r + s + t, then characterizes each of the three determinants as the unique scalar in kappa^* in a displayed relation between two symbols and multiplies the three relations, keeping track of the signs (-1)^{r(s+t)}, (-1)^{rt} and (-1)^{rs} (proof lines 17044-17103). The construction of the admissible sequences and the sign bookkeeping are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
